messages:
Olga: Heads-up — started seeing 200-500ms tail latency spikes on canary under sustained long-context traffic. Roughly aligns with bursts of KV eviction churn. Posting a tiny log sample and stack snippet I grabbed from the canary node:
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:13Z] evicter.cpp:248 evicting 128 entries (hotset 82%)
[2026-03-18T14:02:13Z] pager.cpp:112 page-out triggered, freed 0 pages, reinsert race?
[2026-03-18T14:02:13Z] request.cpp:410 p99 latency spike 338ms
#0  0x7f8a3df92a in Evicter::run()
#1  0x7f8a3dbb12 in thread_main()
```
Anyone else seeing this or a quick hypothesis? :eyes:

deploy-bot: canary deployed: inference-canary/v2026.03.18-evict-heuristics

Sourabh: I pulled a quick flamegraph from the canary host — evicter thread jumps during the bursts, and pager syscall time increases. Flamegraph: https://perf.example.com/fg/abc123

Nina: Did we flip the eviction heuristics or heartbeat throttle in that deploy? I remember PR #1284 changed reinsert/backoff logic for FIFO/LRU alignment.

Alex: I can repro locally with the long-context replay harness (~1000 requests with 16k context). Running the repro now, command: `./tools/repro --workload long_context --concurrency 12 --duration 90s`

Sourabh: Profiling shows eviction ordering non-determinism under concurrent reinserts -> many entries are evicted then immediately reinserted by another thread, causing churn and extra pager work. Batching heuristics probably increase simultaneous eviction candidates which amplifies this.

ci-bot: perf/regressions job 6543 finished — long_context p99 +14% vs baseline, memory churn metric up x2. Logs: https://ci.example.com/job/6543

Nina: Possible quick mitigation: revert heartbeat throttle param introduced in PR #1284 (heartbeat_throttle_ms from 5 -> 50) back to 5ms, or reduce reinsert window so entries reinserted by hot requests aren't immediately eligibile.

Olga: Can we bisect between the kernel-selection/batching PRs and PR #1284? I'm going to pause the canary and roll back the canary param for the evicter until we root cause.

Alex: I'll add deterministic ordering asserts to the evicter repro to try to catch the race. If this is a correctness flaw (ordering), we should fail fast in tests.

Sourabh: Also observed fragmentation spike metrics — lots of small tombstones after reinsert races, which increases memory footprint over long contexts. Quick metric to add: tombstone_count and avg_fragment_size.

Olga: Rolling back canary param now (invoking rollout rollback). Will post after observation window. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary rollback to inference-canary/v2026.03.10 completed (started 14:05Z)

Olga: Post-rollback observation: tail latencies dropped back to baseline within ~2 minutes and pager syscalls dropped. Opening a follow-up issue to triage root cause and add unit/integration tests to assert eviction ordering under concurrent reinserts. Leaving thread open for follow-up.
